description.text: Prospero Lorenzo Lambertini was born on 31 March 1675 in Bologna, the third of five children in a noble family. He studied rhetoric, Latin, philosophy, and theology at the Collegio Clementino in Rome, earning doctorates in sacred and civil law by the age of nineteen. His scholarly reputation led to appointments as a consultor of the Inquisition, promoter of the faith, and canon theologus of the Vatican Basilica, before being created a cardinal in 1726 and later elected pope on 17 August 1740, taking the name Benedict XIV.

As pope, Benedict XIV earned the nickname “the Enlightenment Pope” for his vigorous promotion of scientific learning, the Baroque arts, and the study of the human form. He reformed the Breviary, reduced secular influences, and established the Sacred and Profane Museums, now part of the Vatican Museums. His pontificate also saw the expulsion of the Jesuits from Portugal in 1758, the promulgation of bulls against indigenous slavery in Brazil, and the first papal ban on females serving as altar servers. He died on 3 May 1758 at the age of 83.

curiosities.text: Benedict XIV was known as the “Enlightenment Pope” for his advocacy of science education and his support of anatomical studies at the University of Bologna.
He founded the Sacred and Profane Museums, which later became integral parts of the Vatican Museums, showcasing both religious and secular art.

In 1758, shortly before his death, he ordered the expulsion of the Society of Jesus from Portugal, a move that reflected the papacy’s reluctant compliance with anti-Jesuit demands of European monarchs.
